label: Person
name: Luis Antonio Belluga y Moncada
summary:
Luis Antonio Belluga y Moncada was a prominent Spanish churchman and statesman during the 18th century. Born into the nobility of Valencia, Spain, he rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become Archbishop of Zaragoza in 1735. As a key figure in the Spanish Enlightenment, Belluga y Moncada advocated for education reform and the separation of church and state.

He played a crucial role in shaping the educational policies of King Philip V of Spain, who implemented reforms that would have far-reaching consequences for the country's future development. These reforms included the establishment of free schools, the promotion of scientific inquiry, and the suppression of the Jesuit order.

Belluga y Moncada's legacy can be seen in the continued emphasis on education and secularism in Spanish society. His efforts to promote critical thinking and intellectual freedom paved the way for future generations of thinkers and leaders.

In his later years, Belluga y Moncada became a vocal critic of the Inquisition, arguing that it was a relic of a bygone era that hindered progress and stifled dissent.

As he looked back on his life's work, Belluga y Moncada could take pride in knowing that his efforts had helped to create a more enlightened and secular Spain. His commitment to these ideals would continue to inspire future generations of Spaniards and scholars alike.
